audit.action: cite a better source for the same coding
audit.reasoning: Coding 'fixed final' (rule 01 001 0001 00001) rests on Cândido 2004, the standard and only reference description of Shanenawa (UNICAMP PhD, 264 pp, with a 27-page stress section), corroborated by the same author's 1998 phonology MA. Both were open-access but not held; both fetched sources now to The record's quotation is verbatim at sec. 2.1.4 p.45-46 and Conclusions p.221. Both sources state stress is exceptionlessly word-final, non-contrastive, unaffected by affixation, with compound-internal secondary stress on the left member; the 2004 'quantity-sensitive' wording is analytic only (every word-final syllable is closed), as the record's cite note already says. No competing or later phonological/instrumental study exists (Glottolog n=2, web search nil). Action: fill the empty cite/loc/grade fields with 'Cândido 2004: 45-46, 48 (rule 61), 221

sources.citation: Candido 2004, Descricao morfossintatica da lingua Shanenawa, UNICAMP PhD, full PDF via etnolinguistica.org, sec. 2.1.4 and conclusions; weight discussion is metrical-theory machinery, surface pattern fixed final
sources.quote: independente do numero de silabas de que a palavra e constituida, o acento e sempre predizivel, caindo de forma recorrente na ultima silaba ... o acento sempre se localiza sobre a ultima silaba das palavras, nao podendo, assim, ser considerado um traco distintivo.

sources.citation: Cândido, Gláucia Vieira. 1998. Aspectos fonológicos da língua Shanenawá (Pano). Dissertação de Mestrado, UNICAMP, Campinas. 141 pp. (scanned, no text layer; sec. 4.4 scanned at 150 dpi to)
sources.quote: p.97: 'Os dados em (28) evidenciam que nessa língua, à exceção dos monossilábicos, o acento recai sempre sobre a última sílaba das palavras simples. Trata-se, então, de uma manifestação predizível e que, portanto, não possui função distintiva'; compounds (pp.97-98): stress stays on the last syllable of each member, rightmost carries primary, first member's is weaker (secondary). Purely descriptive (author explicitly declines a metrical analysis, fn. p.96).
sources.locator: sec. 4.4 'O acento', 4.4.1 palavras simples / 4.4.2 palavras compostas, printed pp.96-98 (PDF pp.98-100)
sources.note: The only dedicated phonology of Shanenawa (Glottolog hhtype phonology); independent earlier statement of the same fixed-final pattern (sec. 4.4, pp.96-98). Now fetched sources.
